notes: The San Francisco City Planning Commission's minutes of its regular and special meetings, January to March 1978, from volume 36 of the San Francisco Public Library's deposit at the Internet Archive (36minutesofsanfran1978san). Pages were split from the hOCR search text on the Internet Archive page index, counting the viewer page among the leaves scandata.xml does not mark addToAccessFormats=false, and every page is dated from the meeting header it sits under. Four kinds of finding: what the Commission decided about a property, dated to the meeting that decided it; what the minutes state stood on or occupied the property; dated past facts the minutes state about a building; and landmark actions. A proposal on its own is not a finding. A Board of Supervisors or Board of Permit Appeals action the minutes report without its own date is framed 'by' the date of the meeting that reported it. The minutes name applicants, owners, attorneys, objectors, commissioners and staff throughout; the reader spec (in research/sources/sf-planning-commission-minutes.md, under Reader spec) barred all of them from every field, and kept companies, institutions, named buildings and architects.

coverage.remaining: Every page of volume 36 (36minutesofsanfran1978san, January-March 1978) was read. The volume holds no minutes for the regular meeting of 16 March 1978 (Resolutions 7915-7922, to which three cases were continued) or for the special meeting of 17 February to which the condominium-conversion hearing was continued; they are not in the scan. Next: volume 37 (June-November 1978), then 38-39 (1979-1980) and 40-58 (1994-2005).
coverage.note: 177 OCR pages of minutes text out of 276 viewer pages (278 scanned leaves; from n67 most odd viewer pages are blank versos), read in one session by a single reader with no sub-agents; 19 meetings from 4 January to 23 March 1978 (11 regular, 8 special: the joint open-space hearing with the Recreation and Park Commission of 4 January, the Davies Medical Center evening hearing of 5 January, the residential-zoning text hearing of 19 January, the condominium-conversion hearing of 3 February, and the four district hearings on the proposed residential zoning map of 7, 14, 21 and 28 February and 7 March), each dated from its own header. About two thirds of the text pages are public testimony on the citywide residential rezoning and condominium-conversion policy, which locate nothing. 39 findings: 36 planning decision, 2 occupancy, 1 designation.
